subject.title: fix: resolve Codex fork duplication when parent is unresolved (#2108)

question: Should turn-ID-based parent scoping become the canonical unresolved-parent policy, and should this PR or https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 own the consolidated implementation?
rationale: Current main intentionally defers ambiguous cross-file deduplication, while the two open PRs use different identity and cache-dependency models; choosing the permanent compatibility contract requires maintainer intent after correctness fixes and runtime proof.

options.title: Consolidate one proven branch
options.body: Select one canonical branch, incorporate the compatible identity and cache fixes, resolve both current-head defects, and require redacted cold plus repeated warm corpus proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve fail-open behavior
options.body: Keep current main’s conservative unresolved-parent behavior and pause or close both broader deduplication proposals until copy-stable provenance is demonstrated.

options.title: Sponsor this design narrowly
options.body: Approve turn-ID parent scoping specifically, but require this PR to fix all family transitions and prove upgrade behavior before landing independently.

recommendation.title: Consolidate one proven branch
recommendation.body: Select one canonical branch, incorporate the compatible identity and cache fixes, resolve both current-head defects, and require redacted cold plus repeated warm corpus proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged fork-accounting policy and explicit deferred-work boundary were shaped under this ownership.
